chunks: They have no regard for kinship or treaties with believers, for they are transgressors.

key_terms.الْمُعْتَدُونَ: The transgressors / Those who exceed limits
key_terms.يَرْقُبُونَ: They watch out for / have regard for

ai.seo_question: What does it mean that they 'have no regard for kinship or treaties' in Surah At-Tawbah?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often linked to the Banu Bakr incident, illustrating how polytheists violated the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah to justify war, yet it also serves as a broader criterion for hypocrites who disregard both blood ties (silat al-rahim) and formal covenants (dhimmah). The term 'al-mu'tadun' emphasizes their active transgression of divine limits, marking them as those who initiate injustice against the faithful.
